{{Short description|Normal form for modal logic formulas}}

'''Modal clausal form''', also known as '''separated normal form by modal levels''' (SNF<sub>''ml''</sub>)<ref>{{cite conference |last1=Nalon |first1=Cláudia |last2=Hustadt |first2=Ullrich |last3=Dixon |first3=Clare |date=8 November 2015 |title=A Modal-Layered Resolution Calculus for K |conference=TABLEAUX 2015: Automated Reasoning with Analytic Tableaux and Related Methods, Wrocław, Poland |series= Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=9323 |pages=185–200 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-24312-2_13 |publisher=Springer |doi-access=free |location=Cham |isbn=978-3-319-24312-2}}</ref> and '''Mints normal form''',<ref>{{cite conference |first=Grigori |last=Mints |author-link=Grigori Mints |date=1990 |title=Gentzen-type systems and resolution rules part I propositional logic |conference=COLOG 1988: International Conference on Computer Logic |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=417 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |isbn=978-3-540-46963-6 |doi=10.1007/3-540-52335-9_55 |url-access=subscription |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-52335-9_55}}</ref> is a normal form for [[modal logic]] formulae.

Such a normal form is commonly used for [[automated theorem proving]] using [[tableau calculi]] and [[resolution calculi]] techniques due to its benefits of better space bounds and improved decision procedures. In [[normal modal logic]], any set of formulae can be transformed into an equisatisfiable set of formulae in this normal form.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Goré |first1=Rajeev |last2=Nguyen |first2=Linh Anh |date=12 August 2009 |title=Clausal Tableaux for Multimodal Logics of Belief |url=https://content.iospress.com/articles/fundamenta-informaticae/fi94-1-02 |journal=Fundamenta Informaticae |volume=94 |issue=1 |pages=21–40 |doi=10.3233/FI-2009-115 |url-access=subscription |publisher=Polish Mathematical Society, IOS Press}}</ref>

In [[multimodal logic]] where ''a'' represents an agent corresponding to an accessibility relation function in [[Kripke semantics]], a formula in this normal form is a conjunction of clauses labelled by the modal level (i.e., the number of nested modalities). Each modal level consists of three forms as follows.
* Literal clause: a disjunction of propositional literals <math>\bigvee_{b=1}^r l_b</math>.
* Positive ''a''-clause: <math>l' \to \Box_a l</math> where <math>l'</math> and <math>l</math> are propositional literals.
* Negative ''a''-clause: <math>l' \to \Diamond_a l</math> where <math>l'</math> and <math>l</math> are propositional literals.
These three forms are also called ''cpl''-clauses, ''box''-clauses and ''dia''-clauses respectively.<ref>{{cite conference |title=CEGAR-Tableaux: Improved Modal Satisfiability via Modal Clause-Learning and SAT |last1=Goré |first1=Rajeev |last2=Kikkert |first2=Cormac |date=6 September 2021 |publisher=Springer |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=12842 |pages=74–91 |location=Cham |conference=TABLEAUX 2021: Automated Reasoning with Analytic Tableaux and Related Methods, Birmingham, UK |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-86059-2_5 |doi-access=free |isbn=978-3-030-86059-2}}</ref> Note that any clause in [[conjunctive normal form]] (CNF) is also a literal clause in this normal form.
